card.summary: pandas 3.1.0 removes `pd.read_gbq` and several `pd.read_csv`, `pd.read_table`, `pd.read_excel` and `pd.read_parquet` keyword arguments (`delim_whitespace`, `date_parser`, `infer_datetime_format`, `verbose`, `keep_date_col`, `use_nullable_dtypes`) that were deprecated in 2.x. It also deprecates `float_precision` in the CSV readers, `convert_dates` and `keep_default_dates` in `pd.read_json`, and the 'fastparquet' and 'auto' engines of `pd.read_parquet`.

traps.trap: Passing the `delim_whitespace` keyword to `pd.read_csv` or `pd.read_table` to split on runs of spaces.
traps.instead: Pass the `sep` keyword with the regex `\s+` to `pd.read_csv` or `pd.read_table`.
traps.evidence: Use ``sep="\s+"`` instead.

traps.instead: Pass `parse_dates` together with a `date_format` string to `pd.read_csv`, `pd.read_table` or `pd.read_excel`.
traps.evidence: Use ``date_format`` instead, or read in as ``object`` and then apply :func:`~pandas.to_datetime` as-needed.

traps.instead: Drop the keyword; strict format inference is already the default. Pass `date_format` if the format is known.
traps.evidence: A strict version of this argument is now the default, passing it has no effect.

traps.trap: Calling `pd.read_gbq` to load Google BigQuery data.
traps.instead: Use `pandas_gbq.read_gbq` from the separate pandas-gbq package.
traps.evidence: Please use ``pandas_gbq.read_gbq`` instead.

traps.instead: Omit `float_precision`; every mode now uses the same converter.
traps.evidence: All float precision modes now use the same converter. The ``float_precision`` argument will be removed in a future version.

traps.instead: Pass `dtype=False` to `pd.read_json` to disable type conversion, and parse the date columns yourself after reading.
traps.evidence: Pass ``dtype=False`` to disable type conversion, or parse date columns with :func:`~pandas.to_datetime` after reading.

traps.instead: Pass 'pyarrow' as the `engine`, or omit `engine` to use the default.
traps.evidence: The ``'fastparquet'`` and ``'auto'`` engine options are deprecated. Use ``'pyarrow'`` or do not pass ``engine`` to use the default.

example.explains: Reads whitespace-separated text using `sep` with a regex instead of the removed whitespace flag, parses dates with `parse_dates` and `date_format` instead of a parser callable, and reads a TSV with `pd.read_table` without `float_precision`.
example.code:
import io
import pandas as pd

raw = "date value\n2024-01-05 10\n2024-02-10 20\n2024-03-15 30\n"
# old form used the whitespace flag and a date parser callable; both keywords are removed in 3.1.0
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(raw), sep=r"\s+", parse_dates=["date"], date_format="%Y-%m-%d")
assert list(df.columns) == ["date", "value"]
assert df.shape == (3, 2)
assert df["date"].dtype.kind == "M"
assert df["value"].tolist() == [10, 20, 30]

tsv = "name\tscore\na\t1.5\nb\t2.5\n"
# no float precision keyword: all modes use the same converter in 3.1.0
t = pd.read_table(io.StringIO(tsv))
assert t["score"].tolist() == [1.5, 2.5]
assert t.shape == (2, 2)
print("ok")
